samples.summary: `useSecureCookies()` now answers from GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL, changing four out-of-diff consumers at once
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:250-270) now returns true for an https `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` when `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is unset. Every out-of-diff reader of that answer moves with it: `cliLoginAvailable()` (github-auth.guard.ts:85) and `insecureProductionOrigin()` (github-auth.guard.ts:99), the CLI consent cookie's `secure` flag (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:62), the `returnTo` cookie (login-return-path.ts:95) and the session/refresh cookies (auth.controller.ts:544). Concrete broken combination: an install that serves Wafflebase over plain http (NODE_ENV=development, no GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL because GitHub falls back to the app's registered URL) but sets an `https://` GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL. It now (a) passes the CLI gate that used to refuse it with an actionable 400, and (b) mints `__Host-`/`Secure` session, refresh, state and consent cookies that the http browser silently discards — sign-in stops working with no error anywhere. The diff's own comment argues the change 'only moves towards allowing', which is exactly the direction that removes the fail-closed refusal.

samples.summary: Backend's new `?error=` loopback redirect is not understood by already-installed CLI versions
samples.evidence: `AuthController.githubAuthCallback` now redirects a refused CLI login to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?error=...&state=<nonce>` (auth.controller.ts:219-223). Only the CLI in this diff handles that shape (login.ts:796-805, 837). Any released `wafflebase` binary already on a user's machine takes the old `if (!code) { 400 'Missing code' }` branch, answers 400 and keeps blocking until the five-minute timeout — i.e. the new server-side refusal reaches an unupdated consumer and produces exactly the stranded wait the change exists to remove. No version negotiation guards it.

samples.summary: Integration test user factory creates rows with `emailVerifiedAt` null, now a meaningful state
samples.evidence: `createUserFactory` inserts `{ authProvider: 'github', username, email }` with no `emailVerifiedAt`, so every integration-suite user lands in the 'never proven' population that `UserService.findOrCreateUser` (user.service.ts:135-138) now refuses to merge a second provider into. No current e2e drives an OAuth sign-in, so nothing fails today, but the helper is out of step with the new invariant and the first e2e that exercises sign-in on a pre-made user will get `EmailProviderConflictError` rather than a session.

samples.summary: `UserService.createUser` still creates a user row with no workspace, bypassing the new transactional sign-up
samples.evidence: `createUser(data)` does a bare `prisma.user.create` — no workspace, no membership, no `emailVerifiedAt`, no transaction. It is the exact shape (`user row with no workspace`, `emailVerifiedAt: null`) that `createUserWithWorkspace` (user.service.ts:169-200) was just introduced to make impossible, and it remains a public method on the injected service. It has no callers in `packages/backend/src` today, so this is a latent bypass rather than a live one; either delete it or route it through the same transaction.

samples.summary: Self-hosting and root README env documentation never learned about the GOOGLE_* variables
samples.evidence: The self-hosting env table (self-hosting.md:131-139) and the root README env block (README.md:168-173) both enumerate the OAuth configuration a self-hosted install needs and list only `GITHUB_*`. The new optional `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` / `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` trio — whose absence is precisely why the button never appears and `/auth/google` 404s — is documented only in `packages/backend/README.md:44` and `docs/design/backend.md:861`, neither of which a self-hoster following the documentation package reads. Neither file is covered by the top-level docs/design link check, so nothing flags this.

samples.summary: New exports are used only inside their own file, which knip reports as unused exports
samples.evidence: `OAUTH_REFUSAL_CODES` (auth.types.ts:22) and `OAuthRefusalCode` (auth.types.ts:29) are referenced only by `oauthRefusal` in the same file; `loginRefusalMessage` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:618) is referenced only by the handler in the same file and by no test. knip.json entry sets for `packages/backend` and `packages/cli` do not include these as entry points, so the unused-exports / unused-exported-types lane will name them.

finding.summary: `useSecureCookies()` now answers from GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL, changing four out-of-diff consumers at once
finding.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:250-270) now returns true for an https `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` when `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is unset. Every out-of-diff reader of that answer moves with it: `cliLoginAvailable()` (github-auth.guard.ts:85) and `insecureProductionOrigin()` (github-auth.guard.ts:99), the CLI consent cookie's `secure` flag (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:62), the `returnTo` cookie (login-return-path.ts:95) and the session/refresh cookies (auth.controller.ts:544). Concrete broken combination: an install that serves Wafflebase over plain http (NODE_ENV=development, no GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL because GitHub falls back to the app's registered URL) but sets an `https://` GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL. It now (a) passes the CLI gate that used to refuse it with an actionable 400, and (b) mints `__Host-`/`Secure` session, refresh, state and consent cookies that the http browser silently discards — sign-in stops working with no error anywhere. The diff's own comment argues the change 'only moves towards allowing', which is exactly the direction that removes the fail-closed refusal.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as claimed. `isSecureCookie()` (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:248-260) now returns true for an https `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` when `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is unset (line 257), ahead of the `NODE_ENV` fallback, and is re-exported as `useSecureCookies()` (oauth-state.ts:282-284). Every consumer the reviewer names exists and moves with it: the CLI gate `cliLoginAvailable()` (github-auth.guard.ts:86), enforced as a hard 400 at github-auth.guard.ts:250-262; `insecureProductionOrigin()` (github-auth.guard.ts:99-105); the consent cookie's secure flag (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:62); the returnTo cookie (login-return-path.ts:95); session/refresh cookies (auth.controller.ts:544); plus the `__Host-` prefix and state cookies (oauth-state.ts:63,141,190). The direction of the change is verified by the repo's own tests: github-auth.guard.spec.ts:513-517 asserts the old fail-closed refusal for a development install with no callback URL, while oauth-state.spec.ts:162-170 asserts the new true answer for exactly the dev + https GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL shape — so that install now passes the CLI gate and mints Secure/`__Host-` cookies. Nothing in the repo prevents an http-served origin from carrying an https GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL; the only escape is an operator manually setting COOKIE_SECURE=false (oauth-state.ts:251), which is remediation, not a guard that makes the path unreachable. Note the stale warning/refusal texts (github-auth.guard.ts:253-261, 277-283) still name only GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL/COOKIE_SECURE, reinforcing that the consumer side was not fully updated. Whether the mismatched-scheme deployment is likely is a judgement about probability, not a named refutation ground, so the finding stands under the blast-radius rubric (behaviour change to an exported symbol with out-of-diff consumers, including a loosened fail-closed gate).

finding.summary: `useSecureCookies()` now also answers off `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL`, which silently re-decides two out-of-diff consumers: `cliLoginAvailable()` and `insecureProductionOrigin()`
finding.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:244) now loops over `['GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL','GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL']`, so an `http://` Google callback URL answers the question for an install that configures no GitHub callback URL — a configuration the repo explicitly supports (github-auth.guard.ts:66-76 and packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:472 both describe "no GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL, GitHub falls back to the registered URL"). On such an install with `NODE_ENV=production`, `useSecureCookies()` used to return true; now an `http://` `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` (e.g. behind a TLS-terminating proxy, or copied from the docs' localhost example) flips it to false. The consequences land outside the diff: `cliLoginAvailable()` (github-auth.guard.ts:78-80) starts refusing `wafflebase login` with a 400, `insecureProductionOrigin()` (line 92) starts warning, and `AuthController.baseCookieOptions()` (auth.controller.ts:492) mints session/refresh cookies without `Secure` and without the `__Host-` prefix. The doc block at github-auth.guard.ts:73-76 ("A NODE_ENV=production install with no callback URL is already answered: useSecureCookies() reads it as https") is now false for that case. Fix belongs in the new loop (preferring https over http across the two variables, or keeping GITHUB-only precedence for the NODE_ENV fallback).

verdict.reason: The finding claims `isSecureCookie()` loops over `['GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL','GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL']` so that an `http://` Google callback URL can answer negatively and downgrade `useSecureCookies()` to false. The actual code (oauth-state.ts:248-260) does no such thing: `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is consulted first and answers in both directions (line 253-254), while `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` is read upgrade-only — line 257 short-circuits to `true` ONLY when `callbackScheme(...) === true` (https). An `http://` Google callback returns `false` from `callbackScheme` (line 270), which does not match, so execution falls through to the `NODE_ENV === 'production'` fallback (line 259) and still returns `true`. Hence in the exact configuration the finding describes (no GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL, NODE_ENV=production, http Google callback), `useSecureCookies()` remains `true`, and the claimed out-of-diff consequences at `cliLoginAvailable()` (github-auth.guard.ts:85-87), `insecureProductionOrigin()` (github-auth.guard.ts:99-105) and the session cookie options do not occur. The doc block at github-auth.guard.ts:73-76 is therefore still true, and github-auth.guard.ts:78-83 documents the asymmetry explicitly. A regression test pins this exact case (oauth-state.spec.ts:191-204, asserting true + `__Host-wafflebase_session`). The described code is not present.

finding.summary: `GitHubStrategy.validate` now throws, and the GitHub callback's out-of-diff consumers (CLI loopback wait, frontend `?error=` contract) have no handling for that outcome
finding.evidence: github.strategy.ts:132-137 now throws `UnauthorizedException` when no verified GitHub email is found. That throw happens inside `AuthGuard('github')`, i.e. before `AuthController.githubAuthCallback` runs, so it bypasses the deliberate "redirect back to /login?error=" contract the callback documents (auth.controller.ts:137-157) and the error map in packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:26-35, which has no code for it: the user gets a raw Nest 401 JSON on the backend origin with no way back. For the CLI, `wafflebase login` opens `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli…` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:344) and then blocks on the loopback callback; a 401 in the browser sends nothing to 127.0.0.1, so the command hangs for the full CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS (~5 min, login.ts:857-867). Existing users whose GitHub primary address is unverified also lose access to accounts they can sign into today.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually absent. GitHubStrategy.validate does not throw: at github.strategy.ts:144-146 it RETURNS { authProvider: 'github', error: 'unverified_email' } (return type includes OAuthRefusal, line 129), and the file imports no exception class from @nestjs/common. The controller consumes that value via oauthRefusal (auth.controller.ts:260) and routes it — /login?error= for the browser (auth.controller.ts:166-168) and http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback?error=...&state=NONCE for the CLI (auth.controller.ts:218-223), so the loopback listener does receive something and there is no 5-minute hang. Both claimed-unhandled consumers already carry the code: login-form.tsx:39-42 has an 'unverified_email' entry in LOGIN_ERRORS (plus a generic fallback at :54), and packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:599-609 maps 'unverified_email' in CALLBACK_REFUSALS, surfaced by loginRefusalMessage (:618). The lockout sub-claim also fails: verifiedEmail (github.strategy.ts:58-65) falls back to any other verified address when the primary is unverified. Tests pin all of this (auth.controller.spec.ts:639-647, :681-691; github.strategy.spec.ts:191; packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:101).
